Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that this can be a really overwhelming and emotional time for new mothers, and I'm here to support you every step of the way. 

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential areas where we can offer additional support. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a really valuable way for us to get a sense of how you're doing during this postpartum period.

Please know that everything we discuss today is completely confidential, and I want you to feel safe and supported in sharing your thoughts and feelings with me. I'm here to listen and to offer guidance, not to judge. 

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better sense of your emotional well-being over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible. 

So, let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

(nervously chuckling) Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, like my baby's little facial expressions, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and it's hard to really enjoy things like I used to. Even when my husband tries to make me laugh, it's just not as easy for me to laugh like it was before the baby was born. (pausing, looking down) It's like, I know I should be happy and enjoying this time with my new baby, but it's just feeling really overwhelming and exhausting. (sighing) Sorry, I don't know, it's just been really hard lately.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking head) No, not really. Like I said, it's just not the same. I mean, I'll be playing with my baby, and she'll do something cute, and I'll think to myself, "Oh, that's funny," but it's not like I'm really laughing or feeling happy like I used to. It's more like... (pausing, searching for words) ...I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm doing all the right things, but I'm not really feeling it. And when I do try to laugh or find the humor in things, it feels forced, like I'm just pretending to be happy. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) It's hard to explain, but it just feels like something's missing, you know?
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(sighing) Not really. To be honest, most days I just feel like I'm trying to get through the day, you know? I don't really have the energy or motivation to look forward to things like I used to. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or reading a book, just feel like too much effort now. (shrugging) I mean, I'll think to myself, "Oh, it would be nice to take a walk outside," but then I'll think about all the things I need to do to get the baby ready, and it just feels overwhelming. So, I usually just end up staying home and trying to rest, but even that doesn't really feel restful. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) I just feel really tired and overwhelmed all the time.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Yes... I do that a lot, actually. As a new mom, I feel like I'm supposed to be perfect, and when things don't go right, I automatically think it's my fault. Like, if the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her, I'll think to myself, "I'm a terrible mother, I don't know what I'm doing." Or if I'm not producing enough milk, I'll think, "I'm not good enough, I'm failing my baby." (sighing) It's like, I know it's not rational, but it's just this constant voice in my head that's always criticizing me and making me feel like I'm not doing enough. (pausing, looking up) And it's hard to shake off, you know? It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeling fine, and then something will go wrong, and suddenly I'm just flooded with all these negative thoughts and feelings of guilt and inadequacy. (shaking head) It's really hard to deal with.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yes... all the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, "What if she stops breathing?" or "What if I'm not feeding her enough?" or "What if someone breaks into the house and hurts us?" (shaking head) It's just this constant, nagging voice in my head that's always worrying about something. And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my husband, or my family, or just random things that might happen. (sighing) It's exhausting, to be honest. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And even when I try to calm myself down and tell myself that everything is okay, the worries just keep coming back. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) It's like, I know it's not rational, but I just can't seem to shake it off. Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all these worst-case scenarios, and I'll be awake for hours, just worrying and worrying. (shaking head) It's really hard to deal with.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath) Yes... that's happened to me too. Sometimes I'll just feel this wave of panic come over me, and I don't even know why. It's like, my heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. (shaking head) It's really scary, actually. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes I'll be with my husband or my family, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of panic or fear. (looking down) It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'll be thinking about all these things that could go wrong, and it just feels like everything is spiraling out of control. (pausing, taking a deep breath) And then I'll start to feel like I'm not a good mom, or that I'm not doing enough, and that just makes the panic worse. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) It's really hard to deal with, because I feel like I'm supposed to be strong and capable, but sometimes I just feel so overwhelmed and scared. (voice cracking) And it's hard to talk about, because I don't want to admit that I'm not okay. But... (pausing, taking a deep breath) I guess that's why I'm here, right? To try to get help and feel better.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, and the house, and my relationships... it all just feels so overwhelming. (sighing) Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will be crying, and I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point. (shaking head) And it's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too, like laundry and dishes and grocery shopping. It all just feels so overwhelming, and I don't know how to keep up. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) Sometimes I feel like I'm just drowning in all of it, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I guess that's why I've been feeling so tired and anxious all the time. It's just like, everything is getting on top of me, and I don't know how to make it stop.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone understands) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. It's like, my mind is just racing, and I'm lying there, thinking about everything that's going wrong, and I just can't seem to shut off my brain. (sighing) I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and it just feels like my mind is spinning out of control. (shaking head) And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just lie there, feeling anxious and overwhelmed. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) It's like, I'm just so unhappy, and I don't know how to make it better. I feel like I'm just stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll be lying there, and I'll just start crying, because I feel so overwhelmed, and I don't know what to do. (voice cracking) It's just really hard, you know.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a sense of sadness wash over me) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I just feel so sad and miserable, and I don't know how to make it stop. It's like, I'll be sitting there, holding my baby, and I'll just start crying, because I feel so overwhelmed and unhappy. (shaking head) I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, you know? I'm a new mom, and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my baby, but it's just not feeling that way. (sighing) I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and I'm not really experiencing any joy or happiness. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) And it's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too. Like, I'll be making breakfast, and I'll just start crying, because I'm just so tired and overwhelmed. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I feel like I'm just losing myself, you know? I'm not the same person I used to be, and I don't know how to get back to that person. (voice cracking) It's just really hard, and it feels so lonely. Sometimes I'll have these thoughts, like... (pausing, hesitating) ...like I don't know if I can keep going, or if I'm just too tired to keep trying. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) But I don't want to feel that way. I want to be happy, and I want to enjoy this time with my baby. I just don't know how to make that happen.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just start crying, and I won't be able to stop. (shaking head) It's not just when I'm feeling overwhelmed, either. Sometimes I'll be feeling okay, and then something will just trigger it, and I'll start crying. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) Like, the other day, I was just feeding the baby, and I started thinking about how hard everything is, and I just started crying. (sighing) My husband was trying to comfort me, but I just couldn't stop. I felt like I was just losing control, and I didn't know how to make it stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's just really hard, you know? I feel like I'm just so emotional all the time, and I don't know how to deal with it. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) Sometimes I'll be crying, and I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I just be happy?" (voice cracking) It's just really hard, and it feels so lonely. (starting to cry) I just feel like I'm not doing anything right, and I'm just so tired of feeling this way... (sobbing)
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(nodding slowly, feeling a mix of emotions) Yes... I've had those thoughts. (pausing, looking down) It's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I've wanted to admit to myself or anyone else. But... (sighing) yes, I've had thoughts of self-harm. It's like, when everything feels too much, and I don't know how to make it stop, my mind will just start wandering to these dark places. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) It's not that I want to hurt myself, it's just that sometimes it feels like the only way to escape the pain and the sadness. (shaking head) But I know that's not true, and I know that I need to find other ways to cope. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's just... (voice cracking) it's hard to explain, but sometimes it feels like the only way to make the pain stop. (looking down, feeling a sense of shame) I'm scared to admit it, because I don't want to be judged or thought of as a bad person. But... (sighing) I guess I need to be honest, because I need help. (looking up, eyes pleading) I don't want to feel this way anymore. I want to be happy, and I want to be a good mom to my baby. (voice barely above a whisper) I just don't know how to make it stop.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns, including persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells, which are consistent with the diagnostic criteria for <med>postpartum depression</med>. She reports feeling overwhelmed, anxious, and guilty, with difficulty coping with the demands of motherhood. The patient's responses suggest a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med> and <med>anxiety</med>, with symptoms including <sym>persistent sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, and <sym>guilt</sym>.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 28, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient's response indicates a significant decrease in their ability to laugh and see the funny side of things, as they mention it's 'not like I'm really laughing or feeling happy like I used to' and that it 'feels forced, like I'm just pretending to be happy', which aligns with the option 'Definitely not so much now</sym>, <sym>the 'Hardly at all' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports being anxious or worried all the time, with constant and nagging worries about various things, indicating a high frequency of anxiety.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes frequent and intense feelings of panic and fear, even when surrounded by loved ones, indicating a high level of distress.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>The patient describes having difficulty sleeping due to racing thoughts and feelings of anxiety and overwhelm, indicating a high level of unhappiness that interferes with sleep, matching 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates frequent and uncontrollable crying, even when feeling okay, and an overall sense of emotional overwhelm, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to having thoughts of self-harm, but also expresses a desire not to act on them and a need to find other ways to cope, indicating that these thoughts occur sometimes but not frequently.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms, including <sym>persistent sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, and <sym>guilt</sym>, are consistent with the diagnostic criteria for <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med> as outlined in the <med>DSM-5</med>. The EPDS score of 28 indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>, and the presence of <sym>self-harm thoughts</sym> requires immediate attention and follow-up. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage <med>sleep hygiene practices</med> to improve sleep quality
3. Recommend <med>cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)</med> or other evidence-based treatments for <med>postpartum depression</med>
4. Support patient in developing a <med>safety plan</med> to manage <sym>self-harm thoughts</sym> and ensure patient safety
5. Encourage patient to reach out to <med>support groups</med> or <med>hotlines</med> for additional support and resources
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
